metadata.title: UK Employment Tribunal Backlog Tracker & Regional Wait Times (2026)
metadata.description: Quarterly intelligence tracker analysing Ministry of Justice Employment Tribunal backlogs, regional wait times to preliminary and merits hearings, and employer legal cost exposure across Great Britain.
metadata.source: Ministry of Justice (MoJ) Tribunal Statistics Quarterly and HMCTS Management Information

regions.summaryNote: Longest wait times in Great Britain (~17.8 months to merits). High legal hourly rates (£450 to £700/hr) drive severe employer defence cost escalation.
Heavy case load covering South London, Surrey, Sussex, and Kent (~16.8 months wait time). Judicial capacity constraints cause frequent late listing shifts.
Covers Home Counties and Northern outer London (~16.1 months wait time). Substantial volume of commercial and technology sector redundancy disputes.
One of the busiest provincial hearing centres (~13.8 months wait time). Significant case volume in automotive, logistics, and manufacturing redundancy.
Regional hearing centre for Gloucestershire, Somerset, and wider South West (~13.0 months wait time). Moderate hearing listing flexibility.
Hub for North West commercial claims (~12.5 months wait time). High concentration of corporate finance, media, and tech disputes.
Covers Yorkshire and the Humber (~12.0 months wait time). Active listing management provides relatively predictable preliminary hearing scheduling.
Covers all Welsh unitary authorities (~11.2 months wait time). Bilingual administration options with stable judicial hearing ratios.
Fastest listing in England (~10.8 months wait time). Lower regional backlog allows earlier case management discussions and conciliation windows.

regions.hearingCentre: The Eagle Building, Glasgow & George House, Edinburgh
regions.summaryNote: Separate Scottish jurisdiction (~10.2 months wait time). Distinct procedural rules under Employment Tribunals (Scotland) Regulations with shorter lead times.
